title: Seller's Disclosure Statement
description: New Jersey does not have a mandatory state-specific seller disclosure form by statute. However, the New Jersey Association of Realtors (NJAR) provides a standard Seller's Disclosure Statement that is widely used in practice. Sellers are subject to common law obligations to disclose known latent material defects that are not readily observable.

required_actions.note: While not statutorily required, failure to disclose known material defects may result in common law fraud liability.

title: Consumer Information Statement (CIS)
description: New Jersey real estate licensees must provide the Consumer Information Statement (CIS) at the first substantive meeting with a prospective buyer or seller. The CIS explains the types of agency relationships available and the duties owed by the licensee. Dual agency is permitted with written informed consent.

title: Attorney Review Period (3 Business Days)
description: New Jersey standard residential real estate contracts include a 3-business-day attorney review period. During this period, either party's attorney may review and disapprove the contract, effectively canceling it. The attorney may also propose modifications. If no attorney disapproval letter is sent within the review period, the contract becomes binding. This is not a statutory requirement but is standard contractual practice upheld by courts.

required_actions.note: 3-business-day attorney review period is standard. Either party's attorney may disapprove the contract during this period.

citations: In re Opinion No. 26 of the Committee on the Unauthorized Practice of Law, 139 N.J. 323 (1995)

title: Closing Type — Attorney Required
description: New Jersey is an attorney-closing state. While no single statute mandates attorney involvement, the NJ Supreme Court has established through case law that key closing activities (title examination, document preparation, contract review) constitute the practice of law and must be performed by a licensed attorney. Both buyer and seller typically retain separate attorneys.

required_actions.note: Both buyer and seller should retain separate licensed NJ attorneys for the transaction.

title: Flood Zone and Prior Flood History Disclosure
description: New Jersey requires disclosure of the property's flood zone status and any known prior flooding. The seller must disclose whether the property is located in a FEMA-designated flood zone, whether flood insurance is currently maintained, and any history of flood damage. Post-Sandy legislation strengthened these requirements.

required_actions.note: Include FEMA flood zone designation, flood insurance details, and any known prior flood damage.

title: Bulk Sale / Division of Taxation Notification
description: For all real property transfers, the NJ Division of Taxation must be notified. The buyer is required to withhold a portion of the consideration unless the seller provides a tax clearance letter (GIT/REP forms). This ensures the seller has satisfied all NJ tax obligations.

required_actions.note: Seller must provide completed GIT/REP-1 (resident) or GIT/REP-3 (non-resident). Buyer withholds estimated tax unless clearance letter received.
